coverage.membership_verified_against: The uploaded PDF, not the current live IMDb page.
coverage.filter_policy: Preserve all listed titles, including apparent exceptions to the list description.
limits: Not a complete catalog of every sitcom from these decades.
List inclusion does not establish country, exact runtime, or genre eligibility.
Metadata apart from three noted date corrections is transcribed rather than independently audited.
No personal viewing history, enjoyment, or dislikes were inferred.

data_rules.stable_join_key: All existing IDs remain unchanged. Additional shows use permanent application IDs prefixed later- or seventies-; these are not IMDb IDs.
data_rules.missing_values: Null means unknown or not yet supplied. Missing tags are unannotated, not confirmed absence.
data_rules.tag_semantics: Tags indicate noticeable tendencies or themes, not measured intensity or universal episode content. All show tags are provisional editorial judgments.
data_rules.tag_polarity: Every tag is neutral with respect to personal enjoyment. The same tag can be liked for one show and disliked for another.

confidence_levels.moderate: A plausible series-level annotation that has not been independently verified.
confidence_levels.low: Less certain; prioritize manual review. These labels are not calibrated probabilities.

data_rules.source_precedence: User tag overrides supersede assistant tags; original source snapshot remains preserved.
data_rules.content_caution: Content elements are incomplete descriptive cues, not comprehensive age or content advisories. Identity and social themes are not suitability warnings.
data_rules.personal_tag_reactions: liked_tags and disliked_tags accept IDs from tag_taxonomy; they describe the viewer's reasons within that show, not blanket preferences.
data_rules.rating_scope: Every collection accepts Yes/Meh/No ratings. The seventies shelf overlaps the original collection by ID, so one rating follows the show everywhere.

recommendation_design_notes: No recommendation scores or assumed preferences have been generated.
Begin with content-based similarity after the viewer has supplied ratings; avoid using IMDb popularity or average rating as a substitute for personal taste.
Combine genre-neutral tag overlap with per-show likes/dislikes and factor ratings; a single shared theme should not dominate the result.
Normalize overlap within categories so numerous setting tags do not overwhelm humor or tone. Category weights should be configurable, not treated as learned facts.
Treat unknown presentation features and absent tags as missing evidence, rather than as negative examples.
Keep demographic/identity themes optional in similarity; do not infer sensitive viewer traits or treat identities as objectionable content.
Track how much the viewer saw before treating an overall score as strong evidence. Preserve season/era context and allow revised ratings.
Characters, performance, pacing, and offscreen considerations can matter beyond tag overlap; collect personal notes and factor ratings rather than fabricating numerical show scores.
Recognition signals select the later-show candidate pool. They do not increase personal-match scores; ratings from either collection influence recommendations in both.
